name: Chapter 7: Gravitation
description: Kepler’s laws, universal gravitation, G, variation of g, gravitational potential energy, escape speed, satellites and their energy

cards.term: Who first recognised that all bodies fall with the same constant acceleration?
cards.definition: Galileo (1564–1642), using bodies rolling down inclined planes

cards.term: Geocentric vs heliocentric model: who proposed each?
cards.definition:
Ptolemy: geocentric (~2000 years ago)
Aryabhatta (5th century AD) mentioned a heliocentric model
Copernicus (1473–1543) gave the definitive one

cards.term: Whose observations did Kepler analyse?
cards.definition: Those of his master Tycho Brahe (1546–1601), made with the naked eye

cards.text: Kepler’s law of orbits: all planets move in {{c1::elliptical}} orbits with the Sun at {{c2::one of the foci}}.

cards.term: Perihelion and aphelion?
cards.definition: Perihelion P: closest point to the Sun. Aphelion A: farthest. Semi-major axis a = AP/2

cards.term: How can you draw an ellipse with a string?
cards.definition: Pin the ends at F₁ and F₂ and move a pencil keeping the string taut: F₁T + F₂T = constant

cards.term: An ellipse whose two foci merge is a…?
cards.definition: Circle (semi-major axis = radius)

cards.text: Kepler’s law of areas: the line joining a planet to the Sun sweeps {{c1::equal areas in equal times}}.

cards.term: Law of areas: fast at perihelion, slow at aphelion
cards.definition: Equal areas in equal times because L = mr v⊥ is conserved (central force); small r gives large speed

cards.term: Kepler’s second law follows from which conservation law?
cards.definition: Conservation of angular momentum: ΔA/Δt = L/2m, constant because gravity is a central force

cards.term: Is the law of areas special to the inverse-square law?
cards.definition: No: it holds for any central force

cards.term: Example 7.1: relate the speeds at perihelion and aphelion.
cards.definition: \[m r_P v_P = m r_A v_A \Rightarrow \dfrac{v_P}{v_A} = \dfrac{r_A}{r_P}\]the planet takes longer on the far arc BAC than on CPB

cards.text: Kepler’s law of periods: {{c1::T² ∝ a³}}, where a is the semi-major axis.

cards.term: Table 7.1: what does Q = T²/a³ show for the eight planets?
cards.definition: Q ≈ 3 × 10⁻³⁴ y² m⁻³ for all: the same constant → the law of periods

cards.term: Kepler’s third law in full (circular orbit, radius R)?
cards.definition: \[T^2 = \dfrac{4\pi^2}{GM_S}R^3\]also valid for ellipses with R → a

cards.term: Exercise 7.3: a planet goes round the Sun twice as fast as the Earth. Orbital size?
cards.definition: \[(1/2)^{2/3} \approx\]0.63 times the Earth’s

cards.term: Newton’s moon test: ratio g / a(moon)?
cards.definition: \[\dfrac{g}{a_m} = \dfrac{R_m^2}{R_E^2} \approx 3600\]gravity falls as 1/r²

cards.term: State Newton’s universal law of gravitation.
cards.definition: Every body attracts every other with a force\[F = G\dfrac{m_1m_2}{r^2}\]along the line joining them

cards.term: Vector form of the law?
cards.definition: \[\vec F = -G\dfrac{m_1m_2}{r^2}\hat r\]force on m₁ due to m₂ and on m₂ due to m₁ are equal and opposite

cards.term: Principle of superposition for gravity?
cards.definition:
The net force on a mass is the vector sum of the forces from each other mass.
Each acts as if the others were absent

cards.term: Example 7.2: equal masses m at the corners of an equilateral triangle, 2m at the centroid. Net force on 2m? And if the mass at A is doubled?
cards.definition: Zero (symmetry); with 2m at A: \( 2Gm^2\,\hat j \) (towards A, AG = 1 m)

cards.term: Force between a uniform spherical shell and a point mass outside it?
cards.definition: As if the whole mass were at the centre

cards.term: Force on a point mass inside a uniform spherical shell?
cards.definition: Zero: pulls from different parts cancel

cards.term: Can a body be shielded from gravity (Exercise 7.1a)?
cards.definition: No: a shell gives zero force only from itself; outside bodies still pull. Gravitational shielding is impossible

cards.term: Is the force between two extended bodies along the line joining their CMs?
cards.definition: Not necessarily; it is for spherically symmetric bodies

cards.term: Who first measured G, and when?
cards.definition: Henry Cavendish, 1798

cards.term: Principle of Cavendish’s experiment?
cards.definition:
Big spheres pull small ones on a suspended bar
the gravitational torque twists the wire until\[\tau\theta = \dfrac{GMm}{d^2}L\]measure θ → G

cards.term: Value and SI unit of G?
cards.definition: 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻²; dimensions [M⁻¹ L³ T⁻²]

cards.term: Why is Cavendish said to have "weighed the Earth"?
cards.definition: With G known,\[M_E = \dfrac{gR_E^2}{G}\]follows from g and R<sub>E</sub>

cards.term: g at the Earth’s surface in terms of G?
cards.definition: \[g = \dfrac{GM_E}{R_E^2}\]

cards.term: Example 7.6: find M<sub>E</sub> from g = 9.81, R = 6.37 × 10⁶ m. And from the Moon’s orbit?
cards.definition: 5.97 × 10²⁴ kg from g; 6.02 × 10²⁴ kg from Kepler’s third law — within 1 %

cards.term: Force on a mass m inside the (uniform) Earth at distance r from the centre?
cards.definition: Only the sphere of radius r pulls:\[F = \dfrac{GM_E m}{R_E^3}r\](∝ r)

cards.term: g at height h above the surface?
cards.definition: \[g(h) = \dfrac{GM_E}{(R_E + h)^2} \approx g\left(1 - \dfrac{2h}{R_E}\right)\]for h ≪ R

cards.term: g at depth d below the surface?
cards.definition: \[g(d) = g\left(1 - \dfrac{d}{R_E}\right)\](exact for uniform Earth)

cards.term: Where is g maximum? Its value at the centre?
cards.definition: Maximum at the surface; zero at the centre

cards.term: Trap: for small h and d = h, where is g smaller — at height h or depth h?
cards.definition: At height h: it falls twice as fast (2h/R vs h/R)

cards.term: Exercise 7.16: a body weighs 250 N on the surface. Weight halfway to the centre?
cards.definition: 125 N (g ∝ r inside)

cards.term: Exercise 7.15: 63 N on the surface. Force at height R/2?
cards.definition: 63 × (1/1.5)² = 28 N

cards.term: Exercise 7.2(c): g depends on the mass of the Earth or the mass of the body?
cards.definition: The Earth; g is independent of the body’s mass

cards.term: Teacher addition: effect of Earth’s rotation on g at latitude λ?
cards.definition: \[g_\lambda = g - \omega^2R\cos^2\lambda\]least at the equator, unchanged at the poles

cards.term: Notation: NCERT writes W (and V) for potential energy. What do most books use?
cards.definition: U for potential energy and V for gravitational potential (energy per unit mass). This deck follows that

cards.term: Why is mgh only an approximation?
cards.definition: It assumes g constant; valid only for heights ≪ RE. mgh is the difference in PE near the surface

cards.term: Gravitational PE of two masses at distance r (zero at infinity)?
cards.definition: \[U = -\dfrac{Gm_1m_2}{r}\]

cards.term: Why is gravitational PE negative?
cards.definition: Zero is chosen at infinity and gravity is attractive: work is needed to pull the masses apart to infinity

cards.term: Work done by gravity in moving m from r₁ to r₂?
cards.definition: \[W = -GM_Em\left(\dfrac{1}{r_2} - \dfrac{1}{r_1}\right)\]it depends only on the end points (conservative)

cards.term: Define gravitational potential.
cards.definition: PE per unit mass:\[V = -\dfrac{GM}{r}\](scalar, J kg⁻¹)

cards.term: Gravitational intensity (field) and its relation to g?
cards.definition: Force per unit mass, \( \dfrac{GM}{r^2} \) towards the mass; at the surface it equals g (vector, m s⁻²)

cards.term: PE of a system of many particles?
cards.definition: Sum over all pairs of −Gmᵢmⱼ/rᵢⱼ (superposition)

cards.term: Example 7.3: four masses m at the corners of a square of side l. Total PE and potential at the centre?
cards.definition: \( U = -\dfrac{Gm^2}{l}(4 + \sqrt2) \approx -5.41\dfrac{Gm^2}{l} \); \( V = -\dfrac{4\sqrt2\,Gm}{l} \)

cards.term: Exercise 7.2(d): is −GMm(1/r₂ − 1/r₁) more or less accurate than mg(r₂ − r₁)?
cards.definition: More accurate; mg(r₂ − r₁) holds only near the surface

cards.term: Exercise 7.21: two 100 kg spheres 1.0 m apart. Force and potential at the midpoint? Equilibrium?
cards.definition: Force 0, potential −2.7 × 10⁻⁸ J/kg; unstable equilibrium

cards.term: Escape speed from the Earth’s surface?
cards.definition: \[v_e = \sqrt{\dfrac{2GM_E}{R_E}} = \sqrt{2gR_E} \approx\]11.2 km/s

cards.term: Derive the escape speed idea in one line.
cards.definition: Total energy must be ≥ 0:\[\tfrac12 mv^2 - \dfrac{GMm}{R} \ge 0\]

cards.term: Exercise 7.7: does escape speed depend on the mass of the body or the direction of projection?
cards.definition: No to both; it depends on the location (potential there): slightly on latitude and height

cards.term: Why does the Moon have no atmosphere?
cards.definition: Its escape speed is only 2.3 km/s (≈ 1/5 of Earth’s); gas molecules faster than that escape

cards.term: Example 7.4: spheres M and 4M (radius R), 6R apart. Where is the neutral point, and what minimum speed from M’s surface reaches 4M?
cards.definition: Neutral point 2R from M’s centre;\[v_{min} = \sqrt{\dfrac{3GM}{5R}}\]

cards.term: Exercise 7.18: a body is projected at 3 × escape speed. Speed far away?
cards.definition: \[\sqrt{9 - 1}\,v_e = 2\sqrt2 \times 11.2 \approx\]31.7 km/s

cards.term: Exercise 7.17: rocket fired up at 5 km/s. How far does it go?
cards.definition: To r ≈ 8.0 × 10⁶ m from the centre (≈ 1600 km above the surface)

cards.term: Speed of a satellite in a circular orbit at height h?
cards.definition: \[v = \sqrt{\dfrac{GM_E}{R_E + h}}\]decreases with height, independent of the satellite’s mass

cards.term: Orbital speed close to the surface?
cards.definition: \[v_0 = \sqrt{gR_E} \approx\]7.9 km/s

cards.term: Newton’s cannon: orbital speed vs escape speed
cards.definition: Slow: falls back; v0 = √(gR) ≈ 7.9 km/s: circular orbit; ve = √(2gR) ≈ 11.2 km/s = √2 v0: escapes

advancedHtml.frontHtml:
Orbits · Newton’s cannon

A cannon on a very tall mountain fires horizontally, faster each time. What happens to the ball?

Faster and faster…

cards.term: Relation between escape speed and orbital speed near the surface?
Period of a satellite?
cards.definition: \[T = 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{(R_E + h)^3}{GM_E}}\]→ T² ∝ (R + h)³ (Kepler’s third law)

cards.term: Period of a satellite just above the surface?
cards.definition: \[T_0 = 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{R_E}{g}} \approx\]85 min

cards.term: Moon’s period and a curiosity about it?
cards.definition: 27.3 days, roughly equal to its own spin period, so we always see the same face

cards.term: Example 7.5: Phobos has period 7 h 39 min and orbit radius 9.4 × 10³ km. Mass of Mars? Martian year if its orbit is 1.52 × Earth’s?
cards.definition: 6.48 × 10²³ kg; 684 days (1.52^(3/2) × 365)

cards.term: Example 7.7: k = 10⁻¹³ s² m⁻³ in T² = k r³. Moon at 3.84 × 10⁵ km: period?
cards.definition: k = 1.33 × 10⁻¹⁴ d² km⁻³ → T ≈ 27.3 days

cards.term: Why does an astronaut in an orbiting satellite feel weightless?
cards.definition: Not because gravity is small, but because astronaut and satellite are both in free fall towards the Earth

cards.term: Exercise 7.4: Io’s period 1.769 days, orbit 4.22 × 10⁸ m. Show M(Jupiter) ≈ M(Sun)/1000. Method?
cards.definition: Use M = 4π²R³/(GT²) for Io and for the Earth; the ratio comes to ≈ 1/1000

cards.term: Exercise 7.13: how to "weigh the Sun"?
cards.definition: \[M_S = \dfrac{4\pi^2 R^3}{GT^2}\]with R = 1.5 × 10¹¹ m, T = 1 year → 2.0 × 10³⁰ kg

cards.term: Exercise 7.14: a Saturn year is 29.5 Earth years. Distance from the Sun?
Exercise 7.5: a star 50 000 ly from the centre of a galaxy of 2.5 × 10¹¹ solar masses. Period?
cards.definition: ≈ 3.5 × 10⁸ years

cards.term: Energies of an orbiting satellite
cards.definition: Kinetic energy K: +GMm / 2r; Potential energy U: −GMm / r; Total energy E: −GMm / 2r; Relations: U = 2E,  K = −E

Energy?

Kinetic energy K+GMm / 2r
Potential energy U−GMm / r
Total energy E−GMm / 2r
RelationsU = 2E, K = −E

cards.term: Why must the total energy of a satellite be negative?
cards.definition: It is a bound system; E ≥ 0 would let it escape to infinity

cards.term: Energy needed to take a satellite in orbit (radius r) out of Earth’s influence?
cards.definition: \[+\dfrac{GMm}{2r}\](= −E). Less than for a body at rest at that height (Exercise 7.6b)

cards.term: Exercise 7.19: 200 kg satellite at 400 km height. Energy to escape?
cards.definition: 5.9 × 10⁹ J

cards.term: Raising a satellite from 2R to 4R

advancedHtml.frontHtml:
Example 7.8

Find the missing step.

400 kg satellite moved from orbit radius 2R_E to 4R_E. Energy needed and changes in K and U?
  1. Eᵢ = −GMm/4R, E𝒻 = −GMm/8R
  2. ΔE = GMm/8R = gmR/8 = 3.13 × 10⁹ J
  3. ΔK = −ΔE = −3.13 × 10⁹ J
  4. ?
advancedHtml.backHtml:
Example 7.8

Find the missing step.

400 kg satellite moved from orbit radius 2R_E to 4R_E. Energy needed and changes in K and U?
  1. Eᵢ = −GMm/4R, E𝒻 = −GMm/8R
  2. ΔE = GMm/8R = gmR/8 = 3.13 × 10⁹ J
  3. ΔK = −ΔE = −3.13 × 10⁹ J
  4. ΔU = 2ΔE = +6.25 × 10⁹ J

cards.term: Correction: NCERT Example 7.8 prints ΔV = −6.25 × 10⁹ J. What is the correct sign?
cards.definition:
Positive: Uᵢ = −GMm/2R, U𝒻 = −GMm/4R, so U rises (becomes less negative) by +6.25 × 10⁹ J.
Check: ΔK + ΔU = ΔE = +3.13 × 10⁹ J

cards.term: A satellite loses energy to air drag. What happens to its speed?
cards.definition: It increases: E falls, r shrinks, K = −E rises (Exercise 5.5c)

cards.term: Exercise 7.1(c): the Sun pulls the Earth harder than the Moon does, yet the Moon causes bigger tides. Why?
cards.definition: Tides depend on the difference of pull across the Earth, ∝ M/r³, not M/r²; the nearby Moon wins

cards.term: Exercise 7.1(b): can an astronaut in a very large space station detect gravity?
cards.definition: Yes, through the variation of g across the station (tidal effect)

cards.term: What stays constant for a comet
cards.definition: Linear speed: no; Angular speed: no; Angular momentum: yes; Kinetic energy: no; Potential energy: no; Total energy: yes

cards.term: Exercise 7.9: which symptoms may an astronaut in space get?
cards.definition: Swollen face, headache, orientation problems (body fluids shift upwards); not swollen feet

cards.term: Exercises 7.10–7.11: direction of the gravitational field at the centre C and at a point P on the open face of a hemispherical shell?
cards.definition: Along c and e (straight down): complete the sphere, where the field inside is zero

cards.term: Exercise 7.12: where between the Earth and Sun is the net gravitational force on a rocket zero?
cards.definition: About 2.6 × 10⁸ m from the Earth’s centre

cards.term: Exercise 7.20: two solar-mass stars start at rest 10⁹ km apart. Speed at collision (radius 10⁴ km each)?
cards.definition: ≈ 2.6 × 10⁶ m/s each

cards.term: Conserved quantities under gravity
cards.definition: Angular momentum (about the centre): yes; Total mechanical energy: yes; Linear momentum of the orbiting body: no
